purpose: Define rights/permissions as explicit semantic identities over an action class or operation scope, separate from policy assignments and subject membership.

topics.name: AccessCore Right Identity
topics.purpose: Define rights/permissions as explicit semantic identities over an action class or operation scope, separate from policy assignments and subject membership.

semantics.identity_rule: Each reusable right/permission has an explicit identity.
semantics.operation_rule: Right maps to exact operations/command scopes or declared action classes.
semantics.readwrite_rule: Read/write/mutate/admin/destructive distinctions are explicit rather than implied by naming.
semantics.assignment_rule: Defining a right does not assign it to anyone.
semantics.composition_rule: Composite rights expand only through explicit member refs.
semantics.authority_rule: Right visibility does not grant the right.

invariants.rule: Identity, authentication assurance, authorization policy, authorization decision, delegation and runtime execution remain separate machine-significant identities/evidence; no one layer silently substitutes for another.

Ambiguous, missing, stale or unverifiable authority for a protected effect fails closed rather than inheriting trust from locality, transport reachability, process ownership, UI visibility or previous success.

hard_gates.condition: admin string grants all unknown future commands
